But now the tiling and flooring work has been very slow paced, perhaps since the labour force is limited and they are focusing on Tower 1A to meet the December 2025 RERA timeline. The CRM says they are running as per schedule and are committed to delivering 2B by December 2026 and I'm hoping for 2B work pace to be increased again.
As of now towers 1A, 1B and 2B haven't been assigned official names like Altaire and Celestia towers have.
As for the locality, slowly all slums are being converted to resedential complexes and the general Outlook of the area is improving so the property appreciation is expected to be good.

The builder has significantly delayed possession, and there has been a lack of clear communication or accountability regarding timelines. This is extremely frustrating for buyers who have planned their finances and lives around the promised delivery.

Is anyone else here facing the same issue with delayed possession or unclear updates?

featured_reviews.review_text:
All the promises made by the developer now seem completely misleading. Even their own customer support team has no clarity on when possession will actually be given, nor do they have any proper update regarding the RERA extension.

The original possession was promised for December 2025, but as of now, only basic RCC work has been completed up to a few floors — far from a finished structure.

I’ve also noticed complaints already filed on RERA by other buyers. If there is any existing owners’ group, I request you to please connect with me so we can come together and take collective action for our homes.

It’s extremely disappointing to see such delays, especially considering the poor track record of the developer (Ruparel) in delivering projects on time.

A word of caution to anyone planning to invest — please do thorough research before putting your hard-earned money into such projects.

Kindly share contact details if any group exists.

featured_reviews.name: Abhilasha Jain
featured_reviews.review_text:
Review for Rustamjee Seasons, BKC

If you’re planning to rent or buy here, I’d strongly say: think twice.

The building looks great on the surface with every amenity listed—gym, pool, squash, TT, yoga rooms—but in practice, it’s a disappointment . Here’s why:
1.	Rigid and impractical rules:
•	Table tennis and squash are restricted with sudden, unclear rules—you can’t just go and play when you want.
•	Gym timings are extremely rigid. Management insists the gym cannot open early because the trainer isn’t available, but ironically, the trainer often shows up an hour late even after the gym has officially opened. Makes no sense.
2.	Amenities without basics:
•	The pool is there, but essential float boards or safety equipment are missing. It’s incomplete and not child-friendly.
3.	Hidden charges everywhere:
•	Even after paying steep rents, almost everything is chargeable—yoga rooms, certain common spaces, and more. Feels unfair and exploitative considering the rent is already high.

On top of this, the hygiene is terrible (toilets stink worse than public ones), lifts are painfully slow, and the management is neither flexible nor approachable. If you’re a tenant, your say is practically zero. Even flat owners don’t have much control since the committee runs on its own agenda. And yes parking is scary-no space to even get into the car-forget your car even being cleaned . I think the list is never ending!

Yes, it’s one of the few residential complexes in BKC, but amenities you can’t use and management you can’t reason with cancel out any advantage.

Verdict: Not worth the rent, not worth the stress. Big no from my side.
